_meta.source: Curated from server/rule-engine/rules/ + BOTSv2 scenario coverage
_meta.note: Static subset — when rules change, refresh this file. Keep ≤40 entries to bound prompt token cost.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
techniques.desc: Adversary spawns shell or script interpreter (bash, sh, python, perl) — often reverse shell.

techniques.name: PowerShell
techniques.desc: PowerShell used for execution; often base64-encoded or downloading a remote payload.

techniques.name: Unix Shell
techniques.desc: Unix shell command execution: bash/sh chained with curl/wget for download+execute.

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.desc: wget/curl pulls a payload from an attacker server, usually into /tmp.

techniques.name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files
techniques.desc: base64 -d or echo|base64 pipeline used to decode an embedded payload before execution.

techniques.name: Remote System Discovery
techniques.desc: Enumeration of remote hosts (ping sweep, nmap, ARP scan, arp -a).

techniques.name: File and Directory Discovery
techniques.desc: Filesystem enumeration: find, ls -laR, locate, looking for sensitive content.

techniques.name: SSH Lateral Movement
techniques.desc: SSH client used to move laterally, often with key auth or tunneling for pivot.

techniques.name: Cron
techniques.desc: Write to /etc/cron* or crontab for scheduled execution persistence.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol
techniques.desc: C2 over HTTP/HTTPS/DNS — blends with normal traffic.

techniques.name: Web Protocols (C2)
techniques.desc: HTTP/HTTPS beacon to attacker server; suspicious User-Agent, URI, or POST patterns.

techniques.name: Protocol Tunneling
techniques.desc: Tunneling via ngrok, localtonet, SSH -R/-L to expose internal services.

techniques.name: Non-Standard Port
techniques.desc: C2 over uncommon ports (4444, 1337, etc.) to evade port-based blocks.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over C2
techniques.desc: Data exfiltrated over the existing command channel (HTTP POST, custom protocol).

techniques.name: Exfiltration to Web Service
techniques.desc: Upload to public web service (transfer.sh, pastebin, dropbox) via curl/wget.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Protocol
techniques.desc: python -m http.server or similar opens unauthenticated channel for staging exfil.

techniques.name: Local Data Staging
techniques.desc: Archive staging: tar/zip reads many files then writes a single bundle before exfil.

techniques.name: Credentials In Files
techniques.desc: Read of /etc/shadow, /etc/passwd, .ssh/, aws creds — credential harvesting.

techniques.name: Setuid and Setgid
techniques.desc: chmod u+s on a binary to grant setuid root for later privilege escalation.

techniques.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
techniques.desc: Write to /etc/sudoers or sudoers.d to grant passwordless sudo.

techniques.name: Process Injection
techniques.desc: Injection into another process via ptrace, LD_PRELOAD, or /proc/PID/mem writes.

techniques.name: Proc Memory Injection
techniques.desc: dd or write to /proc/PID/mem — direct process memory injection.

techniques.name: Clear Linux Logs
techniques.desc: Truncate or shred /var/log/* to remove forensic evidence.

techniques.name: File Deletion
techniques.desc: Delete attacker tooling/artifacts (rm -rf /tmp/...) to clean up after intrusion.

techniques.name: Disable or Modify System Firewall
techniques.desc: iptables -F / ufw disable / firewalld stop to remove network defences.

techniques.name: Disable or Modify Linux Audit System
techniques.desc: auditctl -D / rm /etc/audit/rules.d/* — disable host audit logging.

techniques.name: Install Root Certificate
techniques.desc: update-ca-trust + write into /etc/pki/ca-trust to make MITM certs trusted.

techniques.name: Web Shell
techniques.desc: Webserver process (httpd/php) executes a shell — uploaded web shell artefact.

techniques.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
techniques.desc: SQLi / RCE in a web app: suspicious URI patterns like UNION SELECT, ../, ;sh.

techniques.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
techniques.desc: Ransomware: many WRITE events with .crypt/.locked/.encrypted suffix in object name.

techniques.name: Resource Hijacking
techniques.desc: Crypto miner: xmrig/minergate spawn with high CPU, often via pool connection.

techniques.name: Modify Registry
techniques.desc: Registry key written/modified for persistence, config hijack, or disabling security tooling. Look at the key path: Run/RunOnce, Services, Image File Execution Options, AV exclusions.

techniques.name: Registry Run Keys
techniques.desc: Write to HKLM/HKCU ...\CurrentVersion\Run* for autostart persistence.

techniques.name: Windows Service
techniques.desc: Create/modify Windows service via registry under HKLM\System\...\Services\ — persistent backdoor.

techniques.name: Masquerading
techniques.desc: Process/file named to mimic legitimate system tooling (svchost in odd path, lsass copy, system process from /tmp).
